name: Reacquisition of Fiji Citizenship by Former Citizens (dual nationality)

qualifying_event.description: Former Fiji citizens who lost their citizenship by naturalising in another country -- historically common among Indo-Fijians and others who emigrated after the 1987 and 2000 coups, since Fiji did not permit dual citizenship until the 2013 Constitution and the Citizenship of Fiji Act 2009 reversed that position -- may reapply for registration as Fiji citizens while retaining their other nationality.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Current and former Fiji passports; documentation of the prior loss of Fiji citizenship.

requirements.blocker_text: Previously held Fiji citizenship and lost it (typically by naturalising in another country), and now wishes to reacquire it while keeping the other nationality.

evidence_required.document: Oath of Allegiance witnessed by a solicitor/barrister
NZD 2,300 fee (via NZ mission; covers citizenship certificate, oath administration, new passport)

outcome.physical_presence_requirement: no minimum physical presence period stated; a 4-6 month minimum processing timeline applies

sources.title: Fiji High Commission, New Zealand -- Fiji Citizenship: 'The Fiji Government recognizes the existence of dual nationality and permits former-Fiji citizens...to re-apply for Fiji citizenship'; NZD 2,300 fee, Oath of Allegiance witnessed by a solicitor/barrister, criminal-record checks, current and former passports, 4-6 month minimum timeline

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Fiji). STATUS: PUBLISHED -- tier-1 sourced via a Fiji diplomatic mission page. MARQUEE STRUCTURAL FINDING: Fiji's dual-citizenship reversal directly undoes a well-documented historical harm -- under the pre-2009 legal order, naturalising in another country caused AUTOMATIC LOSS of Fiji citizenship, which is the specific mechanism by which many Indo-Fijians and others lost Fijian nationality after emigrating following the 1987 and 2000 coups. This route lets those individuals reclaim citizenship without giving up what they acquired abroad. GENERATIONAL SCOPE, EXPLICITLY UNRESOLVED: this route applies to the former citizens THEMSELVES (first generation, no cap found on how long ago they lost citizenship). It is legally distinct from fj_ancestry_exemption.json (a non-citizenship exemption for descendants, capped at three generations from a 1970 principal citizen) and from fj_citizenship_by_descent.json (registration for children born abroad to a currently-citizen parent). The 2026 Amendment Act text reviewed for this build does NOT address descendant-of-former-citizen registration or state a generational cap for this specific reacquisition route -- if a precise cap exists, it was not found in any tier-1/2 source in this pass.
